jurisdiction.name: Chile
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Chile steers AI through its National AI Policy, first approved by decree in 2021 and updated in 2024 for 2024-2031, and through public-sector guidance: a 2023 circular on AI tools in government, the transparency council's 2024 recommendations on algorithmic transparency (with a May 2026 oversight report on their uptake), and the public procurement agency's AI procurement directive and standard tender terms for AI projects. The 2024 data protection law (Law 21.719), in force from December 2026, adds binding rules on automated decisions and profiling. The education ministry has issued a generative-AI guide and the Supreme Court's 2025 judicial ethics code includes an article on AI. A risk-based AI bill is still before the Senate.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents read in full on official sites, mainly the Ley Chile legislation service. Bills were checked through the Senate's service. Not yet verified from the official text: any AI material from the Chamber of Deputies and the cybersecurity agency. The AI bill, a deepfake bill and the transparency council's planned binding instruction are tracked as leads.

instruments.official_title: Aprueba actualización de la "Política Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial"
instruments.english_title: Decree 12 approving the update of the National Artificial Intelligence Policy (2024 update)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation (Supreme Decree No. 12, signed by the President of the Republic and the Minister of Science)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation
instruments.current_status: In force (Ley Chile marks it 'no derogado'). Signed 11 April 2024 and presented by the Minister of Science on 2 May 2024, but published in the Diario Oficial only on 28 January 2025. The policy PDF, action plan (177 initiatives, 14 ministries; 78% implemented or finished as of April 2025 per MinCiencia) and 2024 results report are linked from the MinCiencia page via Google Drive files. Record re-checked under its existing id; previously titled with the site name only.
instruments.summary: Supreme Decree No. 12 of 11 April 2024, published in the Diario Oficial on 28 January 2025, approves the 2024 update of Chile's National AI Policy and repeals Decree 20/2021. It keeps the three axes (enabling factors; development and adoption; governance and ethics) and the 10-year horizon to 2031, adopts the OECD definition of an AI system, and rewrites the governance and ethics axis after a participatory process (UNESCO RAM methodology and an online consultation), adding sub-axes such as international articulation, environment and climate, inclusion and non-discrimination, children and adolescents, and culture. An action plan of 177 initiatives coordinated by 14 ministries accompanies it.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI policy, the main steering instrument for AI across government.

instruments.current_status: Repealed by article II of Decree 12 (published 28 January 2025). Diario Oficial edition 43119 of 3 December 2021 carries the decree.
instruments.summary: Chile's first National AI Policy, approved by Supreme Decree No. 20 of 20 September 2021 (published in the Diario Oficial on 3 December 2021) and presented in October 2021 with an action plan. It set four cross-cutting principles and three axes (enabling factors such as talent, infrastructure and data; development and adoption; and ethics, regulatory aspects and socio-economic impacts) with a 10-year horizon. It was repealed and replaced by the 2024 update (Decree 12).

instruments.official_title: Ley N° 21.719, que regula la protección y el tratamiento de los datos personales y crea la Agencia de Protección de Datos Personales
instruments.english_title: Law No. 21.719 regulating the protection and processing of personal data and creating the Personal Data Protection Agency
instruments.issuing_authority: National Congress; promulgated by the President of the Republic (Ministry General Secretariat of the Presidency)
instruments.current_status: Published 13 December 2024. Effective date computed from the first transitory article: the amendments to Laws 19.628, 20.285 and 19.496 enter into force on the first day of the 24th month after publication in the Diario Oficial on 2024-12-13. Not yet in force on 12 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Comprehensive reform of Law 19.628 that creates the Personal Data Protection Agency. New article 8 bis gives data subjects the right to object to and not be subject to decisions based on automated processing, including profiling, that produce legal effects or significantly affect them (with contract, consent and legal-authorisation exceptions), and in all such cases requires controllers to ensure information, an explanation, human intervention, the right to express a view and review of the decision. It also defines profiling and requires data protection impact assessments for systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects based on automated processing.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main binding rules on automated decision-making and profiling; governs AI training and use involving personal data.

instruments.official_title: Oficio Circular N° 711: Lineamientos para el uso de herramientas de inteligencia artificial en el sector público
instruments.english_title: Circular Letter No. 711: Guidelines for the use of artificial intelligence tools in the public sector
instruments.issuing_authority: Minister Secretary General of the Presidency and Minister of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation
instruments.current_status: Recommendations (not mandatory); no replacement found as of October 2026. Issued before Law 21.719 reforms Law 19.628. Digital Government Division functions have since moved to the Government Digital Secretariat (Ministry of Finance).
instruments.summary: Joint circular from the Ministry General Secretariat of the Presidency and the Ministry of Science, sent to 309 state bodies, recommending how agencies that develop or use AI tools should act through their digital transformation coordinators. It groups recommendations under people-centred AI (assess whether AI is the right solution, avoid arbitrary discrimination, involve citizens), transparency and explainability (inform the public about AI tools, chatbots and AI-supported decisions), privacy and data use (comply with Law 19.628, do not enter personal or sensitive data into generative AI tools not contracted by the agency, follow security technical standards) and staff training. The Digital Government Division may request information to follow up implementation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main cross-government guidance on public-sector and generative AI use.

instruments.official_title: Resolución Exenta N° 372: Aprueba texto de las recomendaciones del Consejo para la Transparencia sobre transparencia algorítmica
instruments.english_title: Exempt Resolution No. 372 approving the Council for Transparency's recommendations on algorithmic transparency
instruments.issuing_authority: Council for Transparency (Consejo para la Transparencia)
instruments.current_status: In force as recommendations ('no derogado' in Ley Chile). The CPLT published a 'Guía para la adopción de las recomendaciones ... sobre transparencia algorítmica' (PDF on consejotransparencia.cl, file dated January 2025, no date printed). A binding General Instruction on active algorithmic transparency was being prepared (see leads).
instruments.summary: Resolution of 12 August 2024, published in the Diario Oficial on 30 August 2024, approving the Council for Transparency's recommendations on transparency of automated and semi-automated decision systems (SDA), defined broadly to include AI, machine learning and predictive systems that support or replace decisions by public bodies. It recommends that ministries, regional governments, municipalities, armed and security forces and other administrative bodies proactively publish information on SDAs, especially those affecting fundamental rights (e.g. subsidy allocation, school assignment, inspection or sanction processes), and sets criteria for handling reserve or secrecy in access-to-information requests about them.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Chile's main algorithmic transparency standard for the public sector.

instruments.official_title: Directiva de Contratación Pública N° 44/2026: Recomendaciones para la adquisición de proyectos que incluyen ciencia de datos e inteligencia artificial (IA)
instruments.english_title: Public Procurement Directive No. 44/2026: Recommendations for acquiring projects that include data science and artificial intelligence (AI)
instruments.issuing_authority: Directorate of Public Procurement (ChileCompra), Ministry of Finance
instruments.current_status: Directive published 12 March 2026; directives are reference guidance for buyers (art. 10 of the procurement regulation). Resolution point 2 revokes the previous Directive 44 approved by Exempt Resolution 583-B (dated 7 December 2023, although the 2026 text says 'de 2015').
instruments.summary: Exempt resolution (folio 233-B) of 12 March 2026 approving a new version of Directive 44, updated for Law 21.634 modernising Law 19.886 and its new regulation (Decree 661/2024). It guides public buyers procuring data science or AI solutions under any procurement method, especially projects with high technological complexity, personal or sensitive data or automated decisions, recommending multidisciplinary teams, pre-feasibility and risk assessment (privacy, bias, transparency), contract clauses for algorithmic audits, data protection impact assessments and information security, and explainability and citizen participation mechanisms.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current AI procurement guidance for all public buyers.

instruments.english_title: Boost learning: Questions for reflection and practice on generative artificial intelligence in educational settings
instruments.current_status: Launched 12 March 2025 for all schools; in practice it replaces the 2023 teacher guide on ChatGPT.
instruments.summary: Guide for teachers and school teams, prepared by the Ministry of Education's Innovation Centre under the National AI Policy, on integrating generative AI into teaching creatively, critically and responsibly. It sets six principles with reflection questions for using generative AI to teach and learn (including ethical use, privacy and human-centred learning) and proposes practical guidelines and classroom uses, framed as questions rather than fixed rules.

instruments.official_title: Acta N° 244-2025: XXVIII Jornadas de Reflexión de la Corte Suprema; Acuerdo relativo al Código de Ética Judicial
instruments.english_title: Record No. 244-2025: Supreme Court agreement on the Judicial Code of Ethics (article 17 on artificial intelligence)
instruments.current_status: In force as ethical guidance; the code states its prescriptions do not entail legal obligations and are outside the disciplinary regime.
instruments.summary: Supreme Court agreement of 10 November 2025 (published in the Diario Oficial on 19 November 2025) adopting the Judicial Code of Ethics for judges and others exercising jurisdiction. Its article 17 on responsibility in the use of AI and new technologies states that judicial decisions are always human and non-delegable, requires judges to keep meaningful control over and understand the tools they use, lists risks (data leaks, bias, opaque or inaccurate outputs, dependence on vendors), and gives practical rules such as not entering case data into unauthorised public tools, independently verifying AI outputs and citations, and recording any AI support used. The code is ethical guidance and expressly creates no legal or disciplinary obligations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Judiciary's standard for judges' use of AI.

instruments.official_title: Evaluación Transparencia Algorítmica: Informe de Fiscalización Aplicada
instruments.english_title: Algorithmic Transparency Evaluation: Applied Oversight Report
instruments.issuing_authority: Council for Transparency (Consejo para la Transparencia)
instruments.current_status: Dated May 2026 and published on the Council for Transparency's website. It reports an oversight exercise on how central-government bodies apply the 2024 algorithmic transparency recommendations (Resolution 372) and Circular 711 of 2023.
instruments.summary: Oversight report by the Council for Transparency's Oversight Unit (Applied Oversight Area) assessing how public bodies disclose automated and semi-automated decision systems (SDA). It covers access-to-information requests sent on 16 September 2025 to 18 central-administration bodies and a review, between 22 and 30 September 2025, of the ten bodies (nine central-administration bodies and one regional government) that had enabled the 'Transparencia Algorítmica' item on their proactive transparency sites. It finds that ten bodies declared 14 SDA, six bodies breached the access procedure (incomplete or late answers, two partial denials invoking art. 21 of Law 20.285), only three of the ten bodies publish SDA information proactively, and documentation, third-party involvement, audit reports and personal-data protocols vary widely; it restates the obligations under Law 20.285 and General Instruction 10, the Resolution 372 recommendations (publish SDA affecting rights or benefits, monthly updates, plain language), Circular 711 and art. 14 ter of Law 19.628.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Official compliance check of Chile's public-sector algorithmic transparency standard; sets expectations for how bodies must document and disclose AI and automated decision systems.
